text: SENIOR BRIEFING · 12 OCTOBER 2026
Crypto arbitrage tool
Current code and saved evidence reviewed on 12 October 2026. Sources and caveats in speaker notes.
Economics, evidence and the role of bank desks

The current evidence does not
demonstrate a profitable strategy.

Observed spreads do not cover configured costs.
A bank could reduce frictions, but must prove a persistent net edge.

Scope: current local workspace, BSDEX vs World paper engine. Active price feed is Bitstamp plus Binance crypto and EURUSDT; LMAX is a fee proxy. No real orders submitted by this strategy. Current evidence is a 19.35-minute quote file and a documented corrected seven-day candle test, not audited trading P&L. The local backend was unavailable during review.
Project sources: bsdex_strategy.py, config.py, enhanced_signals.py, simulation.py, bsdex_historical_bt.py, docs/engine-integrity.md, ENGINE_INTEGRITY_FIXES.md; data/quotes/2026-10-11.csv.gz.
01 · OPERATING MODEL
The model captures an immediate price difference
Sources: bsdex_strategy.py; simulation.py; config.py.
“BSDEX / LMAX” are labels and fee assumptions. The active price feeds are Bitstamp and Binance.

The active full-depth path uses Bitstamp BTC/EUR and ETH/EUR; the World path uses Binance BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT converted with fresh EURUSDT bid/ask. BSDEX and LMAX labels should not be mistaken for actual execution venues. LMAX fees are configured assumptions applied to Binance-derived prices. The simulator buys and sells the same fixed coin quantity; it does not wait for mean reversion after entry. Prefunding requires both cash and inventory. No actual FX execution, balance debit, partial fill inventory or rebalancing is implemented. Selling USDT proceeds divides by EURUSDT ask; buying divides by bid. Source: bsdex_strategy.py _process_market, _binance_book_usdt_to_eur; simulation.py simulate_arbitrage_trade.

03 · COSTS IN BASIS POINTS
Break even depends on the full execution cost
Sources: config.py; bsdex_historical_bt.py. Fee tiers are assumptions, not verified account quotes.

At €100k, the conservative candle hurdle rises to 19.5 bps
using the > $250M tier, model spread and slippage.
Carry is additional: four pools × 2.50% annually in the current model.

preview: Configured tier | Bitstamp | World proxy | FX | Total

text: 1 bp = 0.01%; at 100,000 EUR, 1 bp = 10 EUR. Exact signal gate compares sale price*(1-sell fee) against buy price*(1+buy fee)+FX cost per coin. FX_COST_BPS=1 is applied once on actual USDT-leg EUR notional. Configured fee tiers: retail <5M 40+6+1=47; >5M 12+6+1=19; >20M default 10+6+1=17; >50M 8+6+1=15; >100M 6+4+1=11; >200M 6+3+1=10; >250M 5+3+1=9; >1B aspirational 3+3+1=7. These are not verified contractual prices. VWAP already includes spread/depth; do not add the candle execution model to quote replay. Conservative candle costs: half-spreads 5+1.5 bps, slippage 2*(capital/100000) bps each leg. At 100k and >250M, approximate mid-price hurdle 9+6.5+4=19.5 bps. Carry=capital*4*.025*hours/8760; four funding pools are an assumption, not regulatory capital. ECB DFR 2.5% effective 16 Sep 2026: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.mp260910~314e508016.en.html .
04 · QUANTITATIVE FRAMEWORK
The z-score finds unusual spreads, not profits
Sources: enhanced_signals.py; config.py; bsdex_strategy.py. Full formula is in the guide.
z = (s − μ) / σ

s  = current spread
μ = recent average spread
σ = typical spread variation

Example: (€5 − €1) / €2 = 2
The spread is two standard deviations
above its recent average.
Why adjust the entry threshold?
The intended response is to demand a more unusual signal when spread volatility or momentum rises.

Live threshold: 0.3–2.0
Base value: 0.4
History: up to 30 recent samples
Limits: volume input is constant; momentum is in raw EUR; predictive value is unproven.

A z-score is the current spread minus its recent average, divided by its standard deviation: z = (s − μ) / σ. It describes an unusual observation, not the probability of profit. The live series is Bitstamp bid minus converted Binance ask in EUR per coin; execution direction is selected separately.
The live threshold is θ = clip[0.4 × (1 + 0.05v) × 1/(1 + ln(2)) × (1 + 0.1|m|), 0.3, 2.0]. v is the standard deviation of spread changes divided by that of spread levels. m is the sum of the latest five spread changes. Volume is supplied as constant 1, making its factor 0.5906; the time factor is 1. Configured windows are 10, 30 and 5 samples, so the processor retains 30. Statistics begin after two observations and include the current observation. The correlation output is unused. Raw EUR momentum is sensitive to the price scale of each coin. These choices need validation.
Sources: enhanced_signals.py; config.py ENHANCED_SIGNAL_SETTINGS; bsdex_strategy.py.
05 · ENTRY CONTROLS AND FREQUENCY
Every signal must pass several gates
Sources: bsdex_strategy.py; enhanced_signals.py; simulation.py.

Live ceiling: about 120 signals/hour per market, not a forecast.
The documented candle test averaged one completed trade per day.

The live loop evaluates approximately every 50 milliseconds and updates statistical signals approximately once per second. Both crypto books and the EURUSDT book must be no more than five seconds old by local receipt time. The z-score, expected net profit and full-depth gates must pass. Quantity is set from capital divided by the Bitstamp mid at signal time.
There is a 30-second cooldown and only one pending order per market. The first eligible evaluation after 300 milliseconds uses current full-size VWAP. Stale or shallow books cause an explicit failure. A negative realized price outcome remains a completed losing trade. This does not model partial leg exposure. The cooldown implies a theoretical ceiling near 120 signals per hour per market, not an expected trade rate. The documented candle run completed seven trades over seven days. No current live-session frequency was available.
Sources: bsdex_strategy.py; enhanced_signals.py; simulation.py.

text: 06 · FULL CYCLE EXAMPLE · ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT A RECORDED TRADE
A valid signal can become a losing fill
Source: current fee and latency model. Example uses 1 BTC, > $250M tier; excludes carry and rebalancing.
Prefund → identify → fix quantity → fill both legs → reconcile and rebalance

preview: One BTC | Signal expectation | Delayed execution

text:
Illustrative arithmetic, not a recorded trade. Assume prefunded cash and coin, one BTC, Bitstamp fee 5 bps, World fee 3 bps and FX cost 1 bp. At the signal, buy at €100,000 and sell at €100,150 after conversion. For example, 112,168 USDT divided by the EURUSDT ask of 1.12 equals €100,150. Fees are €50 + €30.045 + €10.015 = €90.06, leaving expected net profit of €59.94.
If all gates qualify, freeze quantity and direction. At delayed execution, buy at €100,040 and sell at €100,020. Gross loss is €20. Fees are €50.02 + €30.006 + €10.002 = €90.028. Net loss is €110.028, rounded on the slide to €110.03. Signal and fill spreads are about +14.99 and −2.00 bps. Carry and rebalancing are excluded. In a real operation, reconcile and restore inventories after the fill; current simulation omits those actions. A losing fill must not be retrospectively removed.
Sources: simulation.py; bsdex_strategy.py; config.py.
07 · DOCUMENTED BACKTEST RESULT
The corrected candle test lost money
Source: docs/engine-integrity.md, verification dated 11 October 2026; model result, not account P&L.
7 trades  ·  0 winners  ·  7 losses
BTC · 24 Sep–1 Oct 2026 · €100k per leg · > $250M tier · conservative costs

This is the documented corrected public-data run from 11 October 2026, not a new test or account statement. Period: 24 September–1 October 2026 UTC, BTC/EUR, €100,000 per leg, > $250M fee tier, conservative execution costs. Seven trades; no winners. Gross after model execution prices is −€918.4255. Venue and FX fees total €629.5510, including €69.9898 of FX cost. Net is −€1,547.9764. Carry is €191.7808; net after carry is −€1,739.7572. Maximum drawdown is €1,547.9764. Display rounding explains the tiny arithmetic difference.
The old future-fill profitability gate filtered losses and invalidated earlier 100% win-rate claims. Negative gross means removing fees alone cannot make this particular fixed trade set profitable. Different fees could change trade selection. Candle fills use a one-minute lag and model execution costs, so they do not predict a live 300 ms fill exactly. Sharpe is suppressed below 30 trades or 20 days; daily returns include idle days and annualise by √365.
Sources: docs/engine-integrity.md; ENGINE_INTEGRITY_FIXES.md; bsdex_historical_bt.py.
08 · MODEL DIFFERENCES AND EVIDENCE LIMITS
Replay must match live before it predicts live
Sources: enhanced_signals.py; bsdex_historical_bt.py; quote_recorder.py.
One-second recording cannot resolve a 300 ms fill path. The saved 19-minute sample is too short for the quote model’s 60-minute signal window.

preview: Setting | Live paper | Candle replay | Quote replay

text:
The live model retains up to 30 samples, normally around 30 seconds, and includes the current sample. Candle and quote backtests use earlier observations over 60 minutes. Their threshold is fixed at 1.5 and cooldown at 30 minutes, compared with an adaptive 0.3–2.0 threshold and 30-second live cooldown.
Live fills use the first evaluation after 300 ms. Candles use the next bar; quote replay uses the first later snapshot at or after the selected latency, normally one second later with current recording cadence. Quote replay reports missing depth, stale books and excessive gaps as failures. Live sizing is capital divided by Bitstamp mid at signal time; quote sizing uses the signal buy ask; candles use the fill buy price. Quotes preserve top-five depth, while live uses full books. The saved 19.35-minute file is too short for the quote backtest window. It supports spread diagnostics only.
Sources: enhanced_signals.py; bsdex_historical_bt.py; bsdex_strategy.py; quote_recorder.py.
09 · CONDITIONAL INSTITUTIONAL IMPROVEMENTS
Bank desks can reduce specific frictions
Sources: project constraints; ECB and BIS guidance. These are proposals, not secured arrangements.

These are proposals, not verified bank arrangements. Digital assets and electronic execution can provide contracted fees, direct quotes and measured latency, rejects and one-leg exposure. FX can price executable conversion, net flows and assess native-EUR routes where available. EUR/USD does not equal EUR/USDT: stablecoin basis and counterparty risks remain. Treasury and money markets can pool funding and assign real internal transfer prices and balance-sheet charges. Financing and hedging desks can investigate permitted inventory borrow or approved hedges, with residual basis, funding and slippage. Custody, operations and risk must handle reconciliation, transfers, venue limits and kill switches.
BIS guidance supports payment versus payment where practicable and management of remaining settlement exposure. It does not imply that crypto or USDT trades qualify for conventional FX settlement services. The ECB rate supports the model opportunity-cost reference, not a bank borrowing quote.
Sources: project constraints; https://www.bis.org/publ/bcbs241.pdf ; https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.mp260910~314e508016.en.html ; https://www.lmaxdigital.com/trading/ .
10 · DECISION AND NEXT EVIDENCE
Continue as a measured paper pilot
Sources: synthesis of code review and saved results. Further investment depends on measured net economics.
Confirm the real economics
Use contracted venue and FX prices, funding, inventory and rebalancing costs.
Make live and replay comparable
Align the rules; collect longer depth history; measure signal-to-fill deterioration.
Require positive results after every cost
Test out of sample, including failed and partial fills, with clear loss limits.

The proposed next step is a controlled paper pilot because the available evidence does not demonstrate profitability. Confirm actual venue and FX fees, funding, inventory and rebalancing costs. Align warm-up, thresholds, sizing, cooldown and latency across live and replay. Collect a longer quote history with checks for gaps, at a cadence appropriate for the intended execution delay. Measure deterioration between signal and fill. Add partial fills, inventory limits, settlement and kill switches.
Proceed only if results remain positive out of sample after all costs and within acceptable loss and failed-fill limits. In the observed quote sample, maxima of 1.60–2.20 bps cannot cover a 9–17 bps fee hurdle. Lowering the z-score threshold cannot create an economic edge. The companion guide contains the full formula, configured fee tiers and funding caveats.
Sources: synthesis of current code, data/quotes/2026-10-11.csv.gz and docs/engine-integrity.md.
